Wait, `\u006f` is 'o'. That seems very strange. Why would it stop at 'o'?

`\u0020` is space.
`\u006f` is 'o'.
`\u00a0` is non-breaking space.
`\u02ff` is some character.
`\u0370` to `\u0482` are some characters.

If the intention is to match characters that have a single cell width, it should probably include all basic ASCII characters.
ASCII characters go up to `\u007F`.
`\u006f` is only 111.
'p', 'q', 'r', 's', 't', 'u', 'v', 'w', 'x', 'y', 'z' are all after 'o'.
And all uppercase letters are before 'o' (A-Z is 65-90).
But lowercase 'p' through 'z' are 112-122.
So any string containing 'p', 'q', 'r', 's', 't', 'u', 'v', 'w', 'x', 'y', 'z' will fail this regex and take the slow path.
That's definitely a bug!

It should probably be `\u0020-\u007F` for the first range.

Usually, the "fast path" for single-width characters includes most of the basic Latin alphabet and common symbols.
